data.title: Type generation pipeline and System.Text.Json migration

epic.spec:
# Type Generation Pipeline and System.Text.Json Migration

## Overview

Migrate `Uno.Monaco.Editor` from Newtonsoft.Json to System.Text.Json with AOT-compatible source generation, and modernize the dead TypedocConverter-based type generation pipeline to emit STJ-attributed C# from current Monaco typings.

**Current state:**
- 103 files with `using Newtonsoft.Json`, 512+ `[JsonProperty]` attributes, 22 custom converter classes
- TypedocConverter is dead/unmaintained, pinned to `monaco-editor@0.21.3` (vendored runtime is v0.54.0)
- AOT-hostile patterns in `ParentAccessor.cs` (runtime `Type.GetType()` + `DeserializeObject(string, Type)`)
- No STJ usage in application code (fn-1 will introduce first `[JsonSerializable]` context for bridge DTOs)

**Target state:**
- Zero Newtonsoft.Json dependency
- All serialization via STJ source-generated `MonacoJsonContext`
- String-enum converters replaced by `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` (.NET 9+)
- AOT-safe `ParentAccessor` with pre-registered type map
- Modern type generation pipeline emitting STJ-compatible C#

## Scope

**In scope:** STJ migration of all Monaco model types, domain converter rewrites, call-site migration, ParentAccessor AOT redesign, type generation pipeline replacement.

**Out of scope:** Regenerating all Monaco types from 0.54.0 (deferred — generator produces correct output, full regeneration is a follow-up). Test app updates beyond build verification.

## Key decisions

1. **Migration-first approach**: Migrate existing files mechanically, then modernize generator. This is lower risk than regenerating everything at once.
2. **Global CamelCase naming policy** on `MonacoJsonContext` replaces per-property `[JsonPropertyName]` where property names follow PascalCase→camelCase convention. Explicit `[JsonPropertyName]` only for names that don't follow the convention.
3. **Global `DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull`** replaces per-property `NullValueHandling.Ignore`. Properties that MUST serialize null need explicit `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.Never)]`.
4. **ParentAccessor redesign**: Replace `Type.GetType()` + `DeserializeObject(string, Type)` with a `Dictionary<string, JsonTypeInfo>` lookup against the source-gen context.
5. **InterfaceToClassConverter replacement**: Custom `JsonConverter<TInterface>` that delegates to `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<TClass>()` (no `Populate()` equivalent in STJ).
6. **This is a breaking change** — requires major version bump. Newtonsoft.Json transitive dependency removed; `CommandHandler` receives `JsonElement` instead of `JObject`.

## Key references

- BlazorMonaco (STJ-native Monaco wrapper): `serdarciplak/BlazorMonaco` — reference for STJ Monaco patterns
- Telegram.Bot STJ migration: `TelegramBots/Telegram.Bot` — thorough migration reference with source gen
- Uno Platform FontManifest pattern: `unoplatform/uno` `src/Uno.UI/UI/Xaml/FontManifest.cs` — canonical Uno STJ source gen
- [MS migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/migrate-from-newtonsoft)
- [STJ source generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/source-generation)

## Quick commands

```bash
# Verify build after migration
dotnet build MonacoEditorComponent.slnx --no-restore

# Verify both app targets
dotnet build MonacoEditorTestApp/MonacoEditorTestApp.csproj -f net10.0-browserwasm
dotnet build MonacoEditorTestApp/MonacoEditorTestApp.csproj -f net10.0-desktop

# Check no Newtonsoft references remain
grep -r "Newtonsoft" MonacoEditorComponent/ --include="*.cs" --include="*.csproj"
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Zero `using Newtonsoft.Json` in MonacoEditorComponent/
- [ ] Zero `Newtonsoft.Json` in Directory.Packages.props and .csproj
- [ ] `MonacoJsonContext` source-gen context covers all cross-boundary types
- [ ] `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault` set to `false`
- [ ] All string-enum types use `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` (no custom converter classes)
- [ ] `ParentAccessor` is AOT-compatible (no runtime `Type.GetType()`)
- [ ] Build succeeds for `net10.0-browserwasm` and `net10.0-desktop` targets
- [ ] Type generation pipeline emits STJ-attributed C# from monaco.d.ts
- [ ] changelog.md documents breaking change

data.title: Create MonacoJsonContext and STJ serialization infrastructure

tasks.spec:
# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.1 Create MonacoJsonContext and STJ serialization infrastructure

## Description
Create the foundational STJ source-generation context and shared serialization infrastructure that all subsequent tasks depend on.

**Size:** M
**Files:** MonacoEditorComponent/Serialization/MonacoJsonContext.cs (new), MonacoEditorComponent/MonacoEditorComponent.csproj

## Approach

- Create `MonacoJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext` with `[JsonSourceGenerationOptions]`:
  - `PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonKnownNamingPolicy.CamelCase`
  - `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull`
  - `UseStringEnumConverter = true`
- Register all types that cross the JS interop boundary via `[JsonSerializable]`: Position, Range, Selection, CompletionItem, CompletionList, CompletionContext, CodeAction, CodeActionList, CodeActionContext, CodeLens, CodeLensList, Hover, IMarkdownString, ColorInformation, ColorPresentation, IMarkerData, Marker, StandaloneEditorConstructionOptions, IModelDeltaDecoration, IModelDecorationOptions, and collection variants
- Add to .csproj: `<JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>false</JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>`
- Follow Uno Platform pattern from `unoplatform/uno` `FontManifest.cs`
- Context should be `internal partial class` in new `MonacoEditorComponent/Serialization/` directory

## Key context

- fn-1 task 5 creates a separate `BridgeSerializerContext` for desktop bridge DTOs. This context is for Monaco model types. They can be combined later via `JsonTypeInfoResolver.Combine()`.
- `UseStringEnumConverter = true` on the context handles most enum serialization, but enums with non-standard wire names (e.g., `"line-through"`) need explicit `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` attributes (handled in task 2).
- Use `Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` if code content with `<`, `>`, `&` must pass through — STJ escapes these by default unlike Newtonsoft.
## Acceptance
- [ ] `MonacoJsonContext` partial class exists with `[JsonSourceGenerationOptions]`
- [ ] All ~25 cross-boundary types registered via `[JsonSerializable]`
- [ ] `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault` set to `false` in .csproj
- [ ] `dotnet build MonacoEditorComponent.slnx` succeeds (existing Newtonsoft code untouched)
## Done summary

# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.2 Migrate string-enum types to JsonStringEnumMemberName

## Description
Replace all ~22 custom Newtonsoft string-enum converter classes with `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` attributes on enum members. Delete the converter classes.

**Size:** M
**Files:** ~22 enum/converter files in MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/Editor/ and Monaco/Helpers/

## Approach

- For each string-enum converter (e.g., `CursorBlinkingConverter`):
  1. Add `[JsonStringEnumMemberName("wireValue")]` to each enum member
  2. Remove the `[JsonConverter(typeof(XConverter))]` attribute from the enum type (the context's `UseStringEnumConverter = true` handles it)
  3. Delete the converter class
- Known enum files: `AcceptSuggestionOnEnter`, `AutoClosingBrackets`, `AutoClosingOvertype`, `AutoClosingQuotes`, `AutoFindInSelection`, `AutoIndent`, `CursorBlinking`, `CursorStyle`, `CursorSurroundingLinesStyle`, `FoldingStrategy`, `LineNumbersType`, `MatchBrackets`, `Multiple`, `RenderLineHighlight`, `Show`, `SnippetSuggestions`, `TabCompletion`, `WordWrap`, `WrappingIndent`, `TextDecoration`
- Update `using` directives: remove `Newtonsoft.Json` imports, add `System.Text.Json.Serialization`
- Special case: `TextDecoration` has hyphenated values like `"line-through"` — `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` handles this correctly

## Key context

- Pattern: enum `CursorBlinking { [JsonStringEnumMemberName("blink")] Blink, ... }` — no converter class needed
- The `[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))]` per-enum attribute is NOT needed when `UseStringEnumConverter = true` is set on the context (task 1)
- `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` is .NET 9+ — both target frameworks (net9.0, net10.0) support it
## Acceptance
- [ ] All string-enum types have `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` on each member
- [ ] All custom enum converter classes deleted (~22 files)
- [ ] No `[JsonConverter(typeof(XConverter))]` on enum types for string-enum converters
- [ ] `using Newtonsoft.Json` removed from all modified enum files
- [ ] Build succeeds
## Done summary

data.title: Migrate Monaco model JsonProperty attributes to STJ

tasks.spec:
# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.3 Migrate Monaco model JsonProperty attributes to STJ

## Description
Bulk-migrate `[JsonProperty]` attributes to `[JsonPropertyName]` across all Monaco model type files. Update `using` directives and handle `NullValueHandling` patterns.

**Size:** M (mechanical bulk change across ~40 model files)
**Files:** MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/Editor/*.cs, Monaco/Languages/*.cs, Monaco/Helpers/*.cs (~40 files with [JsonProperty])

## Approach

- Replace `[JsonProperty("name")]` with `[JsonPropertyName("name")]`
- For properties where global CamelCase naming policy produces the correct wire name (PascalCase property → camelCase JSON), the `[JsonPropertyName]` can be omitted entirely. Only keep explicit `[JsonPropertyName]` for names that don't follow PascalCase→camelCase convention.
- Remove per-property `NullValueHandling = NullValueHandling.Ignore` — this is handled globally by `DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull` on `MonacoJsonContext`
- For the ~40 properties that currently do NOT have `NullValueHandling.Ignore` (e.g., `[JsonProperty("model")]`, `[JsonProperty("label")]`, `[JsonProperty("insertText")]`), verify they should serialize nulls. If so, add `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.Never)]` to override the global default.
- Replace `using Newtonsoft.Json` with `using System.Text.Json.Serialization`
- Handle `[JsonIgnore]` — same attribute name, different namespace (`System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonIgnore`)
- Handle `private set` on `Range` and `Position` properties — add `[JsonInclude]` on each property with `private set`

## Key context

- `[JsonProperty]` on interfaces (e.g., `IEditorOptions`) — STJ respects `[JsonPropertyName]` on interface members only when the concrete class implements the interface explicitly. Verify this works for `IRange`, `IPosition` etc.
- STJ is case-sensitive by default. The global `CamelCase` naming policy + `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true` on options covers most cases.
- Do NOT touch files that contain enum converters (handled in task 2) or domain converters (handled in task 4).
## Acceptance
- [ ] Zero `[JsonProperty]` attributes in MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/
- [ ] All model types use `[JsonPropertyName]` (only where needed) or rely on CamelCase naming policy
- [ ] `private set` properties on Range, Position have `[JsonInclude]`
- [ ] `using Newtonsoft.Json` removed from all modified model files
- [ ] Properties requiring null serialization have explicit `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.Never)]`
- [ ] Build succeeds
## Done summary
TBD

- Tests:
- PRs:

# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.4 Rewrite domain converters for STJ

## Description
Rewrite the three non-enum custom Newtonsoft converters for STJ: `InterfaceToClassConverter<TInterface, TClass>`, `CssStyleConverter`, and `ColorConverter`.

**Size:** M
**Files:** MonacoEditorComponent/Helpers/InterfaceToClassConverter.cs, MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/Helpers/ICssStyle.cs (contains CssStyleConverter), MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/Languages/ColorInformation.cs (contains ColorConverter)

## Approach

- **InterfaceToClassConverter**: Rewrite as `JsonConverter<TInterface>` where `Read()` delegates to `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<TClass>(ref reader, options)` and `Write()` delegates to `JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, value, typeof(TClass), options)`. No `Populate()` equivalent needed — STJ creates a new instance.
  - Current usage: `IRange→Range`, `IWordAtPosition→WordAtPosition` on properties in `FindMatch`, `ColorInformation`, `IModelDeltaDecoration`
  - Reference: BlazorMonaco `WorkspaceEditJsonConverter` for STJ interface deserialization pattern

- **CssStyleConverter**: Write-only converter. `Write()` outputs `ICssStyle.Name` as a JSON string. `Read()` throws `NotSupportedException`. In STJ, implement as `JsonConverter<ICssStyle>` with `CanConvert` override.
  - Current usage: `[JsonConverter(typeof(CssStyleConverter))]` on `ICssStyle` properties in decoration options

- **ColorConverter**: Rewrite `Windows.UI.Color` ↔ Monaco `{alpha, red, green, blue}` (0-1 floats) using `Utf8JsonReader`/`Utf8JsonWriter`. Map `reader.GetDouble()` for float values and `writer.WriteNumber()` for output.
  - Current usage: `ColorInformation.Color` property

## Key context

- Register all three converters in `MonacoJsonContext` via `[JsonSerializable]` on the types they convert, or add them to `Converters` collection on options.
- STJ custom converters use `ref Utf8JsonReader`/`Utf8JsonWriter` (not `JsonReader`/`JsonWriter`) — different token navigation API.
- CssStyleConverter is write-only: STJ source gen requires both Read/Write to compile, but `Read` can throw `NotSupportedException`.
## Acceptance
- [ ] InterfaceToClassConverter rewritten as STJ `JsonConverter<TInterface>` with Read/Write
- [ ] CssStyleConverter rewritten as STJ `JsonConverter<ICssStyle>` (write-only, Read throws)
- [ ] ColorConverter rewritten as STJ `JsonConverter<Color>` using Utf8JsonReader/Writer
- [ ] All three converters registered in MonacoJsonContext or via [JsonConverter] attributes
- [ ] No `serializer.Populate()` calls remain
- [ ] Build succeeds
## Done summary
TBD

data.title: Migrate serialization call sites and redesign ParentAccessor for AOT

tasks.spec:
# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.5 Migrate serialization call sites and redesign ParentAccessor for AOT

## Description
Migrate all `JsonConvert.SerializeObject`/`DeserializeObject` call sites to `JsonSerializer` with `MonacoJsonContext`, and redesign `ParentAccessor` to eliminate AOT-hostile runtime type resolution.

**Size:** M
**Files:** MonacoEditorComponent/Extensions/WebViewExtensions.cs, MonacoEditorComponent/CodeEditor/CodeEditor.Methods.cs, MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/LanguagesHelper.cs, MonacoEditorComponent/Helpers/ParentAccessor.cs

## Approach

- **WebViewExtensions.cs** (~3 call sites):
  - Replace `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<T>(returnstring)` with `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(returnstring, MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options)`
  - Replace `JsonConvert.ToString(item)` with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(item, MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options)`
  - Replace `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(item, _settings)` with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(item, MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options)`
  - Delete `_settings` field (CamelCasePropertyNamesContractResolver + NullValueHandling.Ignore) — now on context

- **CodeEditor.Methods.cs** (~10 call sites):
  - Replace inline `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(position)` in JS script strings with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(position, MonacoJsonContext.Default.Position)`
  - Use typed `MonacoJsonContext.Default.<Type>` overloads where possible for AOT
  - `AddCommandAsync` line 152: `DeserializeObject<object>` returns `JsonElement` instead of `JObject` — this is a breaking API change, document it

- **LanguagesHelper.cs** (~16 call sites):
  - Replace all `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<T>(args[i])` with `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(args[i], MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options)`
  - Replace `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(result)` with typed serialize calls

- **ParentAccessor.cs** (hardest — AOT redesign):
  - `GetJsonValue()` at line ~177: Replace `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(obj)` with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(obj, obj.GetType(), MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options)`
  - `SetValue(name, value, type)` at line ~266: Replace `Type.GetType(name)` + `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject(value, typeobj)` with a `Dictionary<string, JsonTypeInfo>` lookup:
    - Pre-register known type names from `MonacoJsonContext` at initialization
    - Lookup: `if (typeInfoMap.TryGetValue(typeName, out var typeInfo)) JsonSerializer.Deserialize(value, typeInfo)`
  - Delete `LookForTypeByName` method (assembly scanning) — replaced by static type map
  - The type map can be populated from `MonacoJsonContext.Default.GetTypeInfo(type)` for all registered types

## Key context

- `JsonConvert.ToString(string)` produces a JSON-quoted string (e.g., `"hello"` → `"\"hello\""`). STJ equivalent: `JsonSerializer.Serialize("hello")` produces same output.
- The JS interop pattern `"JSON.parse('" + serialize(obj) + "')"` is sensitive to escaping. Use `JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` on the context to avoid over-escaping `<`, `>`, `&`.
- `ParentAccessor.SetValue` runtime type dispatch is the single hardest migration point. The type registry pattern from `a2aproject/a2a-dotnet` `A2AJsonUtilities.cs` is a good reference.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Zero `JsonConvert.SerializeObject` / `DeserializeObject` calls in codebase
- [ ] Zero `Newtonsoft.Json.JsonSerializerSettings` usage
- [ ] `ParentAccessor.SetValue` uses type info lookup (no `Type.GetType()`)
- [ ] `ParentAccessor.LookForTypeByName` method deleted
- [ ] All serialization uses `MonacoJsonContext.Default.Options` or typed overloads
- [ ] Build succeeds for both TFMs
## Done summary
TBD

# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.6 Remove Newtonsoft.Json dependency and finalize build

## Description
Remove Newtonsoft.Json package dependency entirely, update build artifacts, and verify clean build across all targets.

**Size:** S
**Files:** Directory.Packages.props, MonacoEditorComponent/MonacoEditorComponent.csproj, MonacoEditorComponent/Properties/MonacoEditorComponent.rd.xml, changelog.md

## Approach

- Remove `<PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.4" />` from `Directory.Packages.props:9`
- Remove `<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" />` from `MonacoEditorComponent.csproj:43`
- Update `MonacoEditorComponent.rd.xml` to remove Newtonsoft type directives (lines 15-19) — replace with STJ source-gen trimming hints if needed
- Verify: `grep -r "Newtonsoft" MonacoEditorComponent/ --include="*.cs" --include="*.csproj" --include="*.props"` returns zero results
- Build both targets: `dotnet build MonacoEditorTestApp -f net10.0-browserwasm` and `-f net10.0-desktop`
- Update `changelog.md` with breaking change entry documenting Newtonsoft removal and STJ migration

## Key context

- This is a breaking change for NuGet consumers who depend on the transitive Newtonsoft.Json dependency.
- The `rd.xml` runtime directives file at `MonacoEditorComponent/Properties/MonacoEditorComponent.rd.xml` explicitly references `Newtonsoft.Json.JsonConvert` — these directives are no longer needed with STJ source gen.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Zero `Newtonsoft.Json` references in any .cs, .csproj, or .props file
- [ ] `rd.xml` updated (Newtonsoft directives removed)
- [ ] `changelog.md` documents the breaking change
- [ ] `dotnet build MonacoEditorTestApp -f net10.0-browserwasm` succeeds
- [ ] `dotnet build MonacoEditorTestApp -f net10.0-desktop` succeeds
## Done summary

data.title: Modernize type generation pipeline for STJ output

tasks.spec:
# fn-2-type-generation-pipeline-and.7 Modernize type generation pipeline for STJ output

## Description
Replace the dead TypedocConverter-based type generation pipeline with a modern approach that emits STJ-attributed C# from Monaco TypeScript definitions.

**Size:** M
**Files:** GenerateMonacoTypings/* (rewrite), GenerateMonacoTypings/README.md

## Approach

- Evaluate and select replacement strategy:
  - **Option A**: Fork/patch TypedocConverter to emit STJ attributes instead of Newtonsoft (it has partial STJ support per README)
  - **Option B**: Build a post-processing step that transforms TypedocConverter output (replace `[JsonProperty]` → `[JsonPropertyName]`, etc.)
  - **Option C**: Custom generator using TypeScript compiler API (ts-morph) to read `monaco.d.ts` and emit C# directly
  - **Option D**: Use existing tool like NTypewriter with custom templates

- Update `GenerateMonacoTypings/package.json` to reference `monaco-editor@0.54.0` (match vendored runtime) instead of `@0.21.3`
- Define generated vs. hand-tuned file separation strategy:
  - Generated files get a `// <auto-generated />` header
  - Hand-tuned files (e.g., `StandaloneEditorConstructionOptions` with `INotifyPropertyChanged` + dictionary backing) are NOT overwritten by the generator
  - Use `.generated.cs` suffix or a separate output directory for generated files
- Ensure generated output includes:
  - `[JsonPropertyName]` or relies on CamelCase naming policy
  - `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` on enum members
  - Nullable reference types enabled (replace `--nrt-disabled true`)
  - No Newtonsoft imports
- Update `GenerateMonacoTypings/README.md` with new pipeline documentation
- Test: run pipeline and verify output compiles against `MonacoJsonContext`

## Key context

- TypedocConverter (hez2010/TypedocConverter) last updated 2023-03-29. Supports TS 3.9-4.2. Modern Monaco uses TS 5.x features.
- Current pipeline: `monaco.d.ts` → typedoc → `monaco.json` → TypedocConverter → C# with Newtonsoft attributes
- The version gap (0.21.3 → 0.54.0) means regeneration will produce a different type surface. New types added, some removed/renamed. This is expected.
- `StandaloneEditorConstructionOptions` is heavily hand-tuned with `INotifyPropertyChanged` and `Dictionary<string,object?>` backing — the generator must NOT overwrite it.
- Full regeneration from 0.54.0 is a follow-up task outside this epic — this task sets up the pipeline to be READY for that.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Generation pipeline runs against `monaco-editor@0.54.0` typings
- [ ] Generated C# uses STJ attributes (zero Newtonsoft references)
- [ ] Generated C# enables nullable reference types
- [ ] Generated files marked with `// <auto-generated />` header
- [ ] Hand-tuned files protected from overwrite (separation strategy documented)
- [ ] `GenerateMonacoTypings/README.md` updated with new pipeline docs
- [ ] Pipeline output compiles successfully
## Done summary
TBD
